assessment: All four retained pages were read as text and inspected as rendered pages, including the one map/caption/legend. This is a JPT synopsis, not the full SPE225882 paper. The underlying paper, reference trail, model and operational data remain unverified. Main-PDF reading does not complete the requested underlying-source or reproduction audit.

sections.scope: Title, lead, attribution box, access notice and introduction
sections.assessment: December2025 JPT technical-paper synopsis by Chris Carpenter of SPE225882 by Ali Sabzabadi, Ian Gladman and Bill Billingsley (RISC Advisory). The footer explicitly says the underlying paper has not been peer reviewed. The historic member-access deadline31January2026 is not proof of present availability. Worldwide deployment/targets and regulation are background assertions without a full bibliography here.

Discusses containment, capacity/efficiency, monitoring, capture cost and incentive differences, and SRMS uncertainty/maturity classification. Ownership, geological characterisation and project concept are the three stated maturity components. These qualitative principles do not supply a numerical storage constraint or permission to store cross-border CO2.

Project configuration, Dupuy stratigraphy, water withdrawal/reinjection, containment mechanisms, water-handling limitations, mitigation options and future-performance claims are read. The stated bottleneck is pressure management involving produced-water disposal into the shallower Barrow group, rather than demonstrated failure of CO2 containment. No calibrated operating envelope, pressure threshold or native time series is supplied.

visuals.object: Figure1, location map, caption and three-category legend
visuals.inspection: Caption limits the map to Southeast Asia/Australia in2024. Dark-green=Operational, light-green=Sanctioned, yellow=UnderStudy. Labels read include Arthit, Shepherd, Kasawari, LangLebah, PAU, Vorwata, PNG, Sukowati, Bayu-Undan, Bonaparte, NorthCarnarvon, Reindeer, Gorgon, Moomba, CliffHead, CTSCo and SEA. EGR appears within Sukowati/Vorwata symbols, not as a fourth status-legend class. Kasawari/Shepherd/LangLebah symbols overlap; precise site-symbol attribution needs a larger map/original table and is not silently inferred. Gorgon is shown operational, Moomba sanctioned. These are historical source classifications, not independently checked current project status. No numerical scale or storage capacities are provided.

visuals.object: Table1 referenced in the COMPLETE paper
visuals.inspection: There is no Table1 in this four-page synopsis. The text explicitly attributes the project list to the underlying paper. Its cells/footnotes cannot be declared read from the map.

equations_absence: No displayed formula, numbered equation, derivation, quantitative reservoir model or nomenclature table appears in the four-page synopsis. This does not establish that the underlying full SPE paper has none.
variables: Quantities are narrative rather than defined model variables. Mtpa/Gtpa denote million/billion tonnes per annum; kg/s is instantaneous flow. An annual conversion needs an explicit time/availability basis.

Injection depth is stated as more than7000ft below Barrow Island, and Dupuy gross thickness200–500m. No pressure datum, BHP limit, permeability, well completion, fluid/PVT or sensor depth/time data are supplied.

Reported2Tcf versus120MtCO2 lacks stated standard-volume conditions; no density conversion is adopted. Reported40-year life and storage quantity do not establish a constant annual injectivity ceiling.
Nine CO2-injection wells, four water producers and two water injectors are different services; proposed expansion of water injectors to four must not be interpreted as four CO2 wells.
Qualitative phrases such as order-of-magnitude more complex, good history match and high confidence have no error metric, probability distribution or transferable numerical coefficient here.

claims.claim: Late start, below-target injection and produced-water complexity raise cost/scepticism; principal issue concerns pressure management of the produced-water recipient reservoir.
claims.assessment: This is the authors' interpretation, mediated by a synopsis. It is not independently validated field causality or a quantitative maximum-rate relation.

claims.claim: Thirty–forty operational sites; later40–45 projects vs24in2017; installed44Mtpa; required6.2Gtpa with$4.5trillion investment.
claims.assessment: Definitions and dates differ or are unspecified. The paragraph first sets2050 for6.2Gtpa, then says6.2Gtpa/$4.5trillion by2030. Preserve time-horizon ambiguity and exclude these background values from forward numerical assumptions.

claims.claim: Australia adopted/ratified LondonProtocol in2009 and established ACCUs; potential Asian commercial destination.
claims.assessment: Regulatory context is reported without primary instruments, conditions or current allocated-service evidence. It does not establish permission for this research case.

claims.claim: Containment/capacity/monitoring, source-gas incentives and SRMS framework are important to feasibility and maturity.
claims.assessment: Qualitative points are read; original2017SRMS and2022guidance are not verified. Natural-gas capture being easier than post-combustion is context-dependent and supplies no energy split.

claims.claim: Gorgon about75km offshore;3LNGtrains~16Mt/y; gas14%CO2;3compressor/drying trains;7km pipeline;3drill centres up to9injectors; rates as high150kg/s equivalent4Mt/y.
claims.assessment: Reported configuration only. A continuous365-day conversion of150kg/s gives4.7304Mt/y;4Mt/y may include availability/rounding but the basis is absent. Do not combine these as an independently verified annual service.

claims.claim: Injection beganAugust2019 into late-Jurassic Dupuy, thickness200–500m, >7000ft deep, continuous regional seals; >2Tcf or120MtCO2 over40years.
claims.assessment: Source-reported geology, schedule and capacity expectation; no original logs, volume reference state, permit or model is supplied. Storage expectation is not a measured annual pressure-constrained capacity.

claims.claim: Four water producers and shallower Barrow reinjection balance pressure without producing CO2; aquifers an order of magnitude more complex than depleted fields.
claims.assessment: Pressure-management mechanism is qualitatively reasonable but no balancing equations or containment margin are demonstrated. Complexity phrase is qualitative and excluded as a quantitative factor.

claims.claim: Buoyancy/residual trapping/dissolution/mineralisation retain CO2; no signs of CO2 injectivity issue.
claims.assessment: General mechanisms and project interpretation, not proof of no migration or future leakage. No plume arrays, pressure observations or injectivity diagnostics are provided.

claims.claim: Solids/trace hydrocarbons impaired water-injection wells, reduced water extraction and limited Dupuy pressure reduction and CO2 injection; higher pressure, clay reactivity and lower connected pore volume added limits.
claims.assessment: Read the entire causal chain and distinguish water-well injectivity from CO2 injectivity. Primary produced-water analyses, pressure tests and model counterfactual are needed to validate attribution.

claims.claim: Currently1.6tonnes per year can be sustained.
claims.assessment: The rendered PDF explicitly prints1.6tonnes per year. Context suggests a possible missing multiplier but provides no authoritative correction. Exclude this quantity from calculations; never silently substitute1.6million tonnes/year.

claims.claim: Pressure-management system functions reasonably but below desired rates; invest in water handling subject to approvals; increase water injectors2→4 with horizontal gravel-pack completions, sidetrack existing wells; possibly add CO2 drilling centre/wells.
claims.assessment: Options/plans are not completed installations or validated capacity increases. No costs, approval dates or incremental injection response are quantified.

claims.claim: Starting water extraction with CO2 injection would have discovered treatment issues earlier.
claims.assessment: Reported hindsight counterfactual, not an observed comparison or independently reproduced schedule.

claims.claim: Very good model/observed plume match and high future confidence once water-injection issues are resolved.
claims.assessment: Conditional author conclusion without goodness-of-fit metrics or raw model/observation data in the synopsis. It cannot establish a calibrated reservoir model or guaranteed future performance.

reproduction: The synopsis contains no independently executable model. One transparent unit/calendar check150kg/s×365×24×3600/1e9=4.7304Mt/y is possible and flags the missing annualisation basis; it is not a Gorgon reservoir simulation. Underlying paper/model, pressure/rate histories, completions, water-treatment/injection measurements, fluid/rock properties and calibration/error metrics would be needed to evaluate reported mechanisms and reproduce outcomes.
paper1_use: Qualitative example of coupled CO2/water pressure management, with attribution to a non-peer-reviewed-paper synopsis. Exclude1.6tonnes/year, unsupported numerical complexity factors, unallocated future service and unverified regulatory permission. No Paper1 numerical result is changed.
